items.title: Show HN: I taught Claude Code to file Indian income-tax returns (ITR)
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built and shipped a tool that uses Claude Code to navigate and file complex Indian income-tax returns. It is a prime example of using your exact primary tool to automate a high-friction, real-world task instead of just building another generic chatbot. You can open this repo today to study how they structured their system prompts for complex, multi-step logical rules and apply that same structure to AI-ingest's filtering logic.

items.title: I let Claude Code run my blog for 3 months: numbers and failures
items.why_it_matters: A developer published an honest 3-month retrospective on letting Claude Code manage and run their blog, detailing the exact failure modes, token costs, and where the AI fell short. Reading this will help you anticipate where Claude Code might hallucinate or break your Next.js code as your project grows. Try auditing your current AI-ingest prompt history against their failure list this week to prevent silent bugs in your Supabase integration.

items.title: Show HN: Save your Claude/codex/copilot tokens by using context profiler
items.why_it_matters: Contextspy is a new tool that profiles your Claude, Codex, and Copilot sessions to show you exactly how much useless data (like bloated tool descriptions or massive API responses) is clogging your context window and costing you money. Since you are actively using Claude Code and Codex, this is a direct way to cut your API bill. Try running contextspy on your AI-ingest repository today to identify and trim down your largest context-wasting files.

items.title: Does Speaking to Agents Like Cavemen Save 65% of Tokens? We Test
items.why_it_matters: A hands-on test by JetBrains reveals that writing prompts to AI agents in a stripped-down, 'caveman' style (removing stop words and polite filler) can save up to 65% on token usage without degrading the quality of the output. This is a dead-simple way to stretch your budget while vibe coding. Try stripping all conversational filler from your next three Claude Code prompts today and check your Anthropic billing console to see the immediate token savings.

items.title: Show HN: Relay – turn Claude Code into a visual Kanban build loop
items.why_it_matters: Relay is a new open-source tool that turns your Claude Code terminal sessions into a visual Kanban board, helping you track what the AI is building in real-time. This bridges the gap between terminal-based generation and visual project management, keeping you focused on shipping features. Try installing Relay today and use its visual board to map out and execute the next three API routes you need for AI-ingest.

items.title: Show HN: Ctxdiff – Git diff for your LLM agent's context window
items.why_it_matters: Ctxdiff acts like git diff but specifically for your LLM agent's context window, showing you exactly what information was added, modified, or removed between prompts. This is incredibly useful for debugging why Claude Code suddenly 'forgets' your Supabase schema or Next.js state. Try running ctxdiff during your next debugging session this week to see exactly when your database schema drops out of Claude's active memory.

items.title: Anthropic changed a Claude Code default–how I insulated my framework
items.why_it_matters: A developer documented how a recent silent default change in Claude Code broke their local development framework and shared a simple configuration strategy to insulate your codebase from future tool updates. Since you rely heavily on Claude Code to write your Next.js and Supabase code, keeping your environment stable is critical to shipping. Try applying their config-insulation steps to your local Claude Code settings this week to prevent unexpected framework breaks.

items.title: Show HN: Agent Console – A Local Dashboard for Codex and Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: Agent Console provides a clean, local web dashboard specifically designed to monitor and manage your Codex and Claude Code agent runs in one place. Instead of getting lost in terminal scrollback, you can see your agent's thought process and file changes visually. Try cloning the repo and running it locally today to monitor your next feature build for AI-ingest.
